title: Commerce SDK partner outreach notes
content:
Account: Nebula Commerce (headless commerce + payments)

Quick snapshot
- Vertical: mid-market + enterprise commerce (B2B/B2C hybrid)
- HQ: Denver, ~230 employees, raised Series B 2024
- Primary stack: Node.js microservices, TypeScript frontend, AWS (EKS, RDS)
- Has own checkout + payments connectors (Stripe, Adyen), exploring local gateways in EU/APAC
- Known pain: spikes during promotions -> latency + bot protection; also looking to reduce inference costs for product copy + personalization

Key contacts (sourced from LinkedIn + Crunchbase)
- VP Product: Clara Navar (clara@nebula.com) - owns checkout/merchant experience
- Eng Manager (platform): Mark Hsu - owns SDKs + integrations
- Head of Partnerships: Jonah Keane - affinity deals, integrations

Product fit hypotheses
- Redwood hosted embeddings for search personalization (reduce infra ops; immediate quality improvement vs current TF-IDF)
- On-prem/private for regulated EU merchants who need data residency + custom models
- Dedicated capacity for seasonal spikes to guarantee latency during promotions

Technical constraints (things to confirm)
- Do they allow third-party cloud APIs for PII product copy? What are their PCI/PII requirements? (likely strict for payment flows)
- SDK consumption: they have an npm package for checkout integrations; prefer small, tree-shakeable deps
- Latency SLOs: sub-150ms tail desired for personalization calls in checkout flow

GTM angle bullets (short form)
- Offer: "Plug Redwood embeddings into Nebula search & recommendations with 2-week pilot" (no infra changes for Nebula)
- Business case: reduce cart abandonment by X% (~estimate), speed up QA on marketing copy, lower infra ops burden
- Co-marketing: shared case study on spike-resilience during Black Friday Q4

Outbound email draft — Variant A (short, technical)
Subject: Quick pilot idea for Nebula search personalization
Hi Clara — saw Nebula’s new headless features and thought there’s an easy pilot to dramatically cut search latency and tuning work. Redwood can run a 2-week integration that replaces TF-IDF with embeddings + caching; no infra changes, you keep control of keys/region. Can we do a 20-min sync next week to sketch scope? Samir (Redwood)

Outbound email draft — Variant B (business first)
Subject: Reduce cart drop during peak promos (two-week pilot)
Hi Clara — Congrats on the Series B and the new checkout product. We’ve helped commerce platforms reduce cart abandonment during promo spikes by improving personalization and making model hosting predictable. Would Nebula be open to a short pilot to test impact on a promo cohort? Happy to share a short pilot plan.

Cold call script (30s opener)
- Quick intro + value: "Samir from Redwood — we help commerce platforms keep personalization fast and cheap during spikes. Can I ask 2 quick questions about your checkout personalization?"
- Q1: How are you currently generating product recommendations/personalized copy? (in-house / third-party)
- Q2: Where do you see the most ops/latency pain during promos?

Objection handling (cheat-sheet)
1) "We can't send PII or card data to external APIs"
  - Response: "Totally — Redwood supports private deployment (VPC/on-prem) and KMS integrations. We can keep inference inside your network and only return non-sensitive tokens/ids."
2) "We already have an ML team building models"
  - Response: "Great — Redwood complements in-house models: we can host your model variants with predictable SLAs, provide KV/prefix caching, and help reduce token compute cost so your models are cheaper to run at scale."
3) "Costs look high"
  - Response: "Pilot first — scope a small cohort with strict token limits and Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching) to estimate unit economics. We have examples where dedicated capacity + batching cut token cost by 40–60% for commerce workloads."

Open items / questions to answer in discovery
- Exact data residency/PCI constraints
- Volume estimates for personalization calls (qps + avg tokens)
- Who signs the pilot MSA (legal contact)?
- Ops owner for SDK integration (Mark?)

Next steps (rough timeline)
- 2026-02-24: intro email to Clara (Samir)
- 2026-03-02: 20-min discovery call if interest (Samir + Lina)
- 2026-03-09: draft pilot plan + scope + measurement baseline
- Owner notes: Samir = outreach, Lina = technical follow-up, Ethan = commercial/discount

Notes to self
- Prep 1-pager for pilot that highlights latency SLOs, data residency options, and a pricing guardrail for a 2-week test.
- Pull case study about "promo spike" performance improvements from Redwood biz ops (ask Ethan for numbers).
- Keep email short; Clara responds better to concrete numbers and minimal slides.

Scratchy brainstorm (things to try)
- Offer a "staging mirror" approach: Redwood hosts a read-only mirror of candidate models for A/B during a promo window.
- Suggest a low-friction SDK stub for client-side instrumentation to measure cold vs warm KV/cache hit rates.

---
End of notes.
